subject: History
description: IVC: dates, sites, town planning, decline

questions.stem: INDUS VALLEY CIVILISATION (also Harappan) flourished approximately:
questions.explanation: INDUS VALLEY CIVILISATION (IVC / HARAPPAN): MATURE phase 2600-1900 BCE. Earlier early Harappan ~3300-2600 BCE; Late Harappan ~1900-1300 BCE. Contemporary with EGYPT, MESOPOTAMIA, CHINA — 'cradle' civilisations. DISCOVERY: 1921, HARAPPA (Punjab, now Pakistan) by Daya Ram Sahni; MOHENJO-DARO (Sindh, Pakistan) by RD Banerji 1922; named for first major site. SPREAD: from Afghanistan (Shortugai) to Gujarat + UP — over 2.5 million sq km — LARGEST among contemporary civilisations. Major sites in INDIA: Lothal, Dholavira (Gujarat), Kalibangan (Rajasthan), Banawali, Rakhigarhi (Haryana — possibly LARGEST IVC site). RAKHIGARHI now considered 'capital' candidate.
questions.subject: History

questions.explanation: MOHENJO-DARO = Sindhi for 'MOUND OF THE DEAD' (where bodies / remains were thought to be). DISCOVERED by RD Banerji 1922; excavated by John Marshall (ASI Director-General) + colleagues. KEY FEATURES: GREAT BATH (large public swimming pool, water-resistant — religious purification?); GRANARY (large structure, possibly food storage); CITADEL (raised area for elites); LOWER TOWN (residences, planned grid). NO PALACES, NO TEMPLES (or unidentified) — egalitarian society? UNESCO WHS (1980). HARAPPA — twin city; both lay along then-active SARASWATI / SARASVATI (now dry GHAGGAR-HAKRA). Mohenjo-daro discovered through CHANCE (Buddhist stupa on top led to dig).

questions.stem: DHOLAVIRA (an IVC site in India) is located in which state?
questions.explanation: DHOLAVIRA — Khadir Bet (an island in Rann of Kutch), GUJARAT. UNESCO WORLD HERITAGE SITE since 2021 — INDIA's 40th. Discovered by JP Joshi (1968), excavated extensively by RS Bisht (1989-2005). UNIQUE FEATURES: stone construction (most IVC was brick); 16+ reservoirs (sophisticated WATER MANAGEMENT — vital for arid Kutch); 3-PART city (Castle, Middle Town, Lower Town); 10 INDUS-SCRIPT SIGNS (largest known sign-board, on gateway). Inhabited ~3000-1500 BCE. OTHER major IVC sites in INDIA: KALIBANGAN (Rajasthan; world's earliest ploughed field; fire altars); LOTHAL (Gujarat; world's earliest known DOCKYARD); RAKHIGARHI (Haryana; possibly LARGEST IVC site, ~350 hectares; ancient DNA studies on skeletons).

questions.stem: LOTHAL (Gujarat) is famous as IVC site for its:
questions.explanation: LOTHAL — Gujarat (Bhāl region, near Bhogavo + Sabarmati rivers). Discovered by SR Rao (1957). World's EARLIEST KNOWN DOCKYARD (~2400 BCE): rectangular brick basin (~37×22 m) with sluice gate connecting to river; for boats / cargo handling. Indicates IVC's MARITIME TRADE with Mesopotamia, Persian Gulf — Indus seals + beads found in Sumer. Famous artifacts: TERRACOTTA HORSE figurine (controversial — could rewrite chronology if confirmed), STANDARDISED weights + measures, FIRE altars, BEAD-MAKING workshop. Also has lower town + acropolis. NATIONAL MARITIME HERITAGE COMPLEX being developed at Lothal (announced 2022). NEAR Ahmedabad — easy day-trip.

questions.explanation: INDUS SCRIPT remains UNDECIPHERED despite 100+ years of effort. ~400 SIGNS used; most inscriptions VERY SHORT (avg 5 signs). NO BILINGUAL TEXT (like Rosetta Stone for Egyptian) found yet. Theories: PROTO-DRAVIDIAN, EARLY SANSKRIT, AUSTROASIATIC, or NOT a true language at all (just symbols). KEY scholars: Asko Parpola (Finnish, Dravidian theory), Iravatham Mahadevan (Tamil-Brahmi expert), Steve Farmer (challenges it as language at all). SAMPLE SCRIPT: appears on SEALS (esp. UNICORN motifs — most common on seals, ~60% of seal images), pottery, copper tablets. RECENT: Asko Parpola Indus Project + computational linguistics (entropy analysis suggests structured language); but full decipherment elusive. INDUS SCRIPT is one of world's GREAT undeciphered scripts (along with Linear A, Rongorongo).

options.option_text: Grid layout, drainage system, standardised bricks

questions.explanation: TOWN PLANNING was IVC's hallmark (~4500 years ago!): (1) GRID PATTERN — streets at right angles, N-S + E-W; (2) STANDARDISED bricks (ratio 1:2:4 — uniform across cities, possibly THE world's earliest standardisation); (3) UNDERGROUND DRAINAGE — covered drains, soak pits, regular cleaning provisions; (4) DUAL CITY structure — CITADEL (raised, west, fortified — elites/admin) + LOWER TOWN (east, residential); (5) PUBLIC GRANARIES; (6) WELLS in most houses + public ones; (7) BATHROOMS in each house — IVC had hygiene awareness millennia before others. CONTRAST: Egypt + Mesopotamia of same era didn't have such systematic urban planning. NO MEGA-PALACES + temples (or not identified) → suggests EGALITARIAN, possibly oligarchic society — different from contemporary 'pharaoh-style' civilisations. INDIAN town planners study IVC even today.

questions.stem: DECLINE of IVC (~1900 BCE) is most likely attributed to:

options.option_text: Climate change + drying of Saraswati river system
Single massive earthquake at one site
Plague / pandemic across all sites (option here)

questions.explanation: IVC DECLINE — modern consensus: GRADUAL CLIMATE CHANGE (~2200-1900 BCE) → weakened monsoon → drying of GHAGGAR-HAKRA / SARASWATI river system. Many IVC sites were on this river → without water, urban centres collapsed. Also: shifts in trade routes, possibly increased flooding then drought, soil salinisation (from over-irrigation), declining trade with Mesopotamia. ARYAN INVASION THEORY (proposed by Mortimer Wheeler 1947, popular for decades) is now LARGELY DISCREDITED — no archaeological evidence of mass violence; languages + people shifted gradually. INDO-ARYAN MIGRATION from Central Asia (~1800-1500 BCE) likely peaceful + gradual. Recent ANCIENT DNA studies (Rakhigarhi 2019, Reich Lab) suggest IVC people share ancestry with modern South Asians, with Indo-European steppe ancestry added later. CULTURAL CONTINUITY: many IVC elements likely persist in modern Indian culture.
